title: Psalms Chapter 77 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 77 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 77 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 77.

questions.question: To whom is Psalms 77 directed as the chief musician?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeduthun
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:1 states that the psalm is to the chief musician, to Jeduthun.

questions.question: What did the psalmist do with his voice according to Psalms 77:1?
questions.correctAnswer: He cried unto God
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:1 says, 'I cried unto God with my voice, even unto God with my voice.'

questions.question: In Psalms 77:2, when did the psalmist seek the Lord?
questions.correctAnswer: In the day of trouble
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:2 says, 'In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 77:2, the psalmist's sore ceased at night.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:2 states, 'my sore ran in the night, and ceased not,' indicating it did not cease.

questions.question: What did the psalmist's soul refuse to be in Psalms 77:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Comforted
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:2 says, 'my soul refused to be comforted.'

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 77:3, the psalmist was troubled when he remembered God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:3 says, 'I remembered God, and was troubled.'

questions.question: What happened to the psalmist's spirit in Psalms 77:3?
questions.correctAnswer: It was overwhelmed
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:3 says, 'my spirit was overwhelmed.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 77:4, what effect did trouble have on the psalmist's eyes?
questions.correctAnswer: Held them waking
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:4 says, 'Thou holdest mine eyes waking.'

questions.question: True or False: In Psalms 77:4, the psalmist was so troubled that he could not speak.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:4 states, 'I am so troubled that I cannot speak.'

questions.question: What did the psalmist consider in Psalms 77:5?
options: The days of old and years of ancient times
questions.correctAnswer: The days of old and years of ancient times
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:5 says, 'I have considered the days of old, the years of ancient times.'

questions.question: In Psalms 77:6, what did the psalmist call to remembrance?
questions.correctAnswer: My song in the night
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:6 says, 'I call to remembrance my song in the night.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask about the Lord in Psalms 77:7?
options: Will the Lord cast off forever?
Will the Lord bless the land?
Will the Lord speak to the nations?
questions.correctAnswer: Will the Lord cast off forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:7 says, 'Will the Lord cast off for ever? and will he be favourable no more?'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 77:7 expresses doubt about whether the Lord will remain favorable.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:7 questions if the Lord will be favourable no more, showing doubt.

questions.question: In Psalms 77:6, besides calling to remembrance his song, what else does the psalmist do?
options: Communes with his own heart and his spirit made diligent search
questions.correctAnswer: Communes with his own heart and his spirit made diligent search
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:6 states, 'I commune with mine own heart: and my spirit made diligent search.'

questions.question: In Psalms 77, which action comes first?
options: The psalmist remembered God and was troubled
The psalmist called to remembrance his song in the night
The psalmist cried unto God with his voice
The psalmist considered the days of old
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist cried unto God with his voice
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:1 shows that the first action is the psalmist crying unto God with his voice before remembering God or calling to remembrance his song.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 77 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 77 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 77:8, what concern does the psalmist express about God's mercy and promises?
options: That his mercy and promises will last forever
That his mercy is gone forever and his promises fail forevermore
That his mercy is conditional upon sacrifices
That his promises are only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: That his mercy is gone forever and his promises fail forevermore
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:8 explicitly asks if God's mercy is gone forever and if His promises fail forevermore, expressing the psalmist's deep distress and doubt.

questions.question: What two questions in Psalms 77:9 express the psalmist's fear about God's grace and mercy?
options: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has He in anger shut up His tender mercies?
Will God punish the wicked? Will He forsake the righteous?
Does God hear our prayers? Does He answer all?
Is God slow to anger? Is He full of compassion?
questions.correctAnswer: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has He in anger shut up His tender mercies?
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:9 directly asks if God has forgotten to be gracious and if He has shut up His tender mercies in anger, highlighting the psalmist's spiritual struggle.

questions.question: How does the psalmist resolve his doubts in Psalms 77:10?
options: He decides to forget past troubles
He acknowledges his infirmity but chooses to remember the years of God's power
He accepts that God has abandoned him
He prays for immediate relief without reflection
questions.correctAnswer: He acknowledges his infirmity but chooses to remember the years of God's power
questions.explanation: In Psalms 77:10, the psalmist admits his weakness ('this is my infirmity') but commits to remembering 'the years of the right hand of the most High,' showing faith despite doubts.

questions.question: What does Psalms 77:11 say the psalmist will remember, and why is this important for faith?
options: The works of the LORD and His wonders of old, to strengthen faith
The failures of others, to avoid their mistakes
Only his own prayers, to gain comfort
The laws of the land, to stay obedient
questions.correctAnswer: The works of the LORD and His wonders of old, to strengthen faith
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:11 expresses the psalmist's intention to remember God's past works and wonders, which is important for sustaining faith during trials (verses 10-12).

questions.question: According to Psalms 77:12, how does the psalmist engage with God's works?
options: He meditates on them and talks of God's doings
He ignores them in his sorrow
He writes laws based on them
He compares them to other gods
questions.correctAnswer: He meditates on them and talks of God's doings
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that the psalmist meditates on all God's work and talks about His doings, highlighting active reflection and testimony as ways to maintain trust.

questions.question: What does Psalms 77:13 teach about God's presence and greatness?
options: God's way is in the sanctuary, and none is so great as our God
God only cares for the righteous
God's greatness is hidden from men
questions.correctAnswer: God's way is in the sanctuary, and none is so great as our God
questions.explanation: Verse 13 declares that God's way is in the sanctuary and questions who is as great as our God, emphasizing His greatness and holy presence.

questions.question: How does Psalms 77:14 describe God’s character and His relationship with people?
options: God is a God who does wonders and declares His strength among the people
questions.correctAnswer: God is a God who does wonders and declares His strength among the people
questions.explanation: Verse 14 highlights God's wondrous acts and His declaration of strength among the people, reinforcing trust in His power and care.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith can a believer learn from the psalmist’s declaration in Psalms 77:11-12?
options: Remembering and meditating on God's past works strengthens faith during hardships
Ignoring past experiences helps avoid confusion
Faith depends solely on present feelings
questions.correctAnswer: Remembering and meditating on God's past works strengthens faith during hardships
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 teach that recalling and reflecting on God's past deeds encourages perseverance and trust in difficult times.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 77:8-9, the psalmist fully trusts that God's mercy and promises will never fail.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 show the psalmist questioning whether God's mercy and promises have ended, reflecting doubt rather than full trust.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 77:10-11, how does the psalmist respond to his doubts about God's mercy?
options: By remembering the right hand of the Most High and His works
By blaming others for his troubles
questions.correctAnswer: By remembering the right hand of the Most High and His works
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 show the psalmist confronting his infirmity by recalling God's powerful acts as a source of hope.

questions.question: What does Psalms 77:13-14 teach about the nature of God that can encourage believers facing uncertainty?
options: God is uniquely great, does wonders, and reveals His strength to His people
God only cares for some nations
questions.correctAnswer: God is uniquely great, does wonders, and reveals His strength to His people
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 affirm God's unmatched greatness and His active working among His people, encouraging trust amidst doubt.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist in Psalms 77:10-12 encourages believers to forget past troubles and focus only on present feelings.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The psalmist encourages remembering God's works and meditating on them (verses 10-12), rather than ignoring the past or dwelling only on feelings.

questions.question: How does Psalms 77:8-10 illustrate the process of dealing with spiritual doubt?
options: By expressing honest questioning but choosing to remember God's power
questions.correctAnswer: By expressing honest questioning but choosing to remember God's power
questions.explanation: Verses 8-10 show the psalmist honestly questioning God's mercy but then deciding to remember God's mighty deeds, modeling how to confront doubt with faith.

questions.question: What does Psalms 77:14 say God has done among the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Declared His strength
questions.explanation: Verse 14 states that God has declared His strength among the people, showing His active involvement and power.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 77:8-9, the psalmist is certain that God's promises and mercy have ended forever.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks if God's mercy and promises have ended, indicating uncertainty and questioning rather than certainty (verses 8-9).

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 77 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 77.

questions.question: According to Psalms 77:15, by what means has God redeemed His people?
questions.correctAnswer: With His arm
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:15 states explicitly, 'Thou hast with thine arm redeemed thy people,' indicating God's powerful deliverance through His strength.

questions.question: In Psalms 77:16, what was the reaction of the waters to God?
questions.correctAnswer: They were afraid
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'The waters saw thee, O God... they were afraid,' showing the fearful response of the waters to God's presence.

questions.question: Psalms 77:17 describes the skies sending out what?
questions.correctAnswer: A sound
questions.explanation: The verse reads, 'the skies sent out a sound,' indicating the audible manifestation of God's power in nature.

questions.question: Which natural phenomena are described in Psalms 77:18 as manifestations of God's power?
questions.correctAnswer: Thunder, lightnings, earth trembling
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:18 describes 'The voice of thy thunder... the lightnings lightened the world: the earth trembled and shook,' highlighting God's awe-inspiring power.

questions.question: What is meant by the phrase 'Thy way is in the sea, and thy path in the great waters' in Psalms 77:19?
options: God’s mysterious and powerful work in the Red Sea crossing
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mysterious and powerful work in the Red Sea crossing
questions.explanation: This verse alludes to God's miraculous guidance through the sea, especially the Exodus event, where His path was unknown to men but evident in deliverance.

questions.question: Who does Psalms 77:20 say God led His people by?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses and Aaron
questions.explanation: The verse states clearly, 'Thou leddest thy people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron,' indicating the leadership during the Exodus.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event is most directly evoked by Psalms 77:19-20?
questions.correctAnswer: The Exodus from Egypt
questions.explanation: The imagery of God's way in the sea and leading by Moses and Aaron clearly recalls the Exodus event (Exodus 14), where God parted the Red Sea to deliver Israel.

questions.question: Psalms 77:16-18 contain vivid imagery describing God’s power over nature. What literary device is primarily used here?
questions.correctAnswer: Personification
questions.explanation: The waters 'saw' God and were afraid, clouds 'poured out water', and arrows went abroad, attributing human actions and feelings to natural elements, which is personification.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'redeemed' in Psalms 77:15 most closely means:
options: To rescue or deliver by a powerful act
questions.correctAnswer: To rescue or deliver by a powerful act
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root for 'redeemed' (ga’al) often means to rescue or deliver, especially in the context of God’s saving acts for Israel (Psalms 77:15).

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 77:15-20 emphasize God’s deliverance of Israel through miraculous acts in nature.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: These verses describe God's wonders and power over waters, storms, and leading His people, highlighting miraculous deliverance (Psalms 77:15-20).

questions.question: What question does the Psalmist ask concerning God's mercy in Psalms 77:8?
options: Is his mercy clean gone forever?
Is his mercy new every morning?
questions.correctAnswer: Is his mercy clean gone forever?
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:8 asks, 'Is his mercy clean gone for ever?' expressing the Psalmist’s doubt and seeking reassurance of God's enduring mercy.

questions.question: How does Psalms 77:11-12 demonstrate the Psalmist’s method of coping with distress?
options: By remembering and meditating on God's past works
questions.correctAnswer: By remembering and meditating on God's past works
questions.explanation: Verses 11-12 show the Psalmist choosing to recall and meditate on God's wonders and doings as a source of comfort.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God leading His people like a flock as in Psalms 77:20?
options: John 10:11 - Jesus as the Good Shepherd
Romans 8:28 - All things work together for good
Revelation 21:4 - New heaven and new earth
questions.correctAnswer: John 10:11 - Jesus as the Good Shepherd
questions.explanation: John 10:11 describes Jesus as the Good Shepherd who leads and cares for His sheep, paralleling the shepherd imagery in Psalms 77:20.

questions.question: True or False: The Psalmist in Psalms 77 expresses certainty that God has abandoned His people forever.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Though the Psalmist questions God’s favor (Psalms 77:7-9), he ultimately chooses to remember God's mighty works and mercy, showing hope rather than certainty of abandonment (Psalms 77:10-12).

questions.question: How does Psalms 77:14 describe God's power among the people?
options: He has declared His strength among the people
questions.correctAnswer: He has declared His strength among the people
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'thou hast declared thy strength among the people,' indicating a public demonstration of God's power.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 77 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 77 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express about God's attentiveness in his distress?
options: God gave ear to his voice
questions.correctAnswer: God gave ear to his voice
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:1 states that the psalmist cried unto God with his voice and that God gave ear unto him, showing God's attentiveness in times of trouble.

questions.question: According to Psalms 77:2, how did the psalmist describe his soul during his suffering?
questions.correctAnswer: Refused to be comforted
questions.explanation: The psalmist says in Psalms 77:2 that his soul refused to be comforted despite seeking the Lord in his trouble, indicating deep anguish and unrest.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most highlighted by the psalmist's question in Psalms 77:8 about mercy and promise?
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:8 questions whether God's mercy and promise have failed forever, which addresses God's immutability—His unchanging nature in promises and mercy.

questions.question: What do Psalms 77:10-11 reveal about the psalmist’s approach to spiritual infirmity?
options: He focuses on past divine faithfulness
He blames God for his condition
questions.correctAnswer: He focuses on past divine faithfulness
questions.explanation: In Psalms 77:10-11, the psalmist acknowledges his infirmity but chooses to remember the mighty works and right hand of the Most High, showing reliance on God's faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Psalms 77:13 describe God's unique nature among deities?
options: God's way is in the sanctuary and He is incomparable
God is limited by human understanding
questions.correctAnswer: God's way is in the sanctuary and He is incomparable
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:13 declares that God's way is in the sanctuary and asks who is so great a God as our God, emphasizing His holiness and uniqueness.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 77:5-6 and Psalms 77:11 convey about divine remembrance and human meditation?
options: Human memory is unreliable and God forgets
Remembering God's works leads to spiritual renewal
questions.correctAnswer: Remembering God's works leads to spiritual renewal
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:5-6 shows the psalmist searching his heart and remembering old days, while 77:11 affirms remembering the LORD's works, together teaching that meditation on God's past deeds renews faith and hope.

questions.question: According to Psalms 77:15, which act of salvation is attributed to God's strength?
options: Redeeming the sons of Jacob and Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: Redeeming the sons of Jacob and Joseph
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:15 states that God, with His arm, redeemed His people, specifically the sons of Jacob and Joseph, highlighting His saving power.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by the imagery of thunder, lightning, and trembling earth in Psalms 77:18?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s omnipotence
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:18 describes the voice of thunder, lightning, and the trembling earth, all manifestations of God's overwhelming power, indicating His omnipotence.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by comparing Psalms 77:19 and Psalms 77:20 about God's guidance?
options: God’s path is hidden but He leads His people personally
God abandons His people in the wilderness
God’s guidance is unpredictable and chaotic
God leads only through visible signs
questions.correctAnswer: God’s path is hidden but He leads His people personally
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:19 notes God's way is in the sea and His path in great waters with unknown footsteps, while 77:20 shows God leading His people like a flock by Moses and Aaron’s hand, indicating hidden yet personal guidance.

questions.question: How does the psalmist express his emotional state in Psalms 77:4?
options: He is joyful and at peace
He is so troubled that he cannot speak
He is indifferent to his circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: He is so troubled that he cannot speak
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:4 says the psalmist's eyes are held waking because he is so troubled that he cannot speak, indicating deep emotional distress.

questions.question: What apologetic response does Psalms 77:7-9 provide against the sceptic's claim that God has permanently rejected His people?
options: It confirms God’s rejection is permanent
It questions but ultimately affirms God's ongoing mercy
It denies any divine mercy or promise
questions.correctAnswer: It questions but ultimately affirms God's ongoing mercy
questions.explanation: Though Psalms 77:7-9 voice doubts about God's favor and mercy, the psalmist later affirms God's faithfulness (Psalms 77:10-11), showing that apparent rejection is temporary, countering sceptic claims.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the psalmist’s reliance on remembering God's 'right hand' in Psalms 77:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of divine providence
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:10 shows the psalmist remembering the years of the right hand of the Most High, symbolizing God's providential power and care throughout history.

questions.question: What does Psalms 77:16-17 reveal about God's relationship with creation during His acts of power?
options: Creation is indifferent to God's actions
Creation responds in fear and turmoil
questions.correctAnswer: Creation responds in fear and turmoil
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:16-17 describes waters being afraid, depths troubled, clouds pouring water, and skies sending sound, showing creation’s fearful response to God's mighty acts.

questions.question: How does Psalms 77:12 demonstrate the psalmist’s spiritual discipline?
options: Meditating and speaking of God's works
questions.correctAnswer: Meditating and speaking of God's works
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:12 states the psalmist will meditate on all God's work and talk of His doings, demonstrating disciplined reflection and proclamation of divine acts.

questions.question: What combined theological truth emerges from Psalms 77:3 and Psalms 77:9 about human suffering and divine mercy?
options: Human complaint coexists with trust in mercy despite doubts
Divine mercy is absent during suffering
Suffering is caused by divine abandonment
questions.correctAnswer: Human complaint coexists with trust in mercy despite doubts
questions.explanation: Psalms 77:3 shows the psalmist's troubled and overwhelmed spirit, while 77:9 questions God's graciousness but retains hope, illustrating that lament and trust coexist in faith.
